speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly how your right groin pain started and what specific position your leg was in during the rear-end collision. Also, have you noticed any inability to move your leg or feel numbness in your thigh or foot?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Femoral Neck Fracture. The patient's history of a rear-end collision causing immediate severe right groin pain, combined with her age and the specific mechanism of injury, is highly suggestive of a femoral neck fracture. Immediate imaging is required to confirm the diagnosis and plan treatment. REQUEST IMAGES: X-ray Pelvis AP and Lateral.
